title: Streaming resume semantics and sensible retry profiles for SDK libraries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Clients across Python/TypeScript/Go have divergent retry/backoff defaults and ambiguous streaming resume behaviors. This causes inconsistent application-level duplicates, expensive fallbacks, and poor developer UX when streams are interrupted.

Goal: Define cross-SDK defaults and conventions that: 1) minimize accidental duplicate operations, 2) make streaming retry/resume predictable and ergonomic, and 3) provide concrete examples for language SDKs and server-side guidance.

Scope: defaults for non-streaming and streaming RPCs, idempotency key naming and lifecycle, a retryable error taxonomy (transport vs server vs application), stream-resume token model, and examples for Python, TS, and Go SDKs. Not in scope: server-side runtime changes; this ticket focuses on SDK behavior and guidance for server teams.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-language default retry profiles defined (fast-fail P0, standard P1, aggressive P2) with explicit parameters for initial_delay, max_delay, multiplier, and jitter strategy.
Canonical idempotency header names and recommended semantics documented for both unary and streaming APIs (including guidance on whether server must persist stream resume tokens).
Retryable error taxonomy published with concrete mappings to HTTP/gRPC codes and common SDK exceptions for Python/TS/Go.
Streaming resume contract: explicit semantics, when to resume vs restart, and SDK helper utilities for token management with code examples in all three languages.
Backward-compatibility guidance and a migration path for customers using previous SDK versions.
PRs for SDKs (python-sdk, js-sdk, go-sdk) opened with a prototype shim and unit tests that validate default profiles and header propagation.
tasks: Draft RFC documenting profiles, headers, taxonomy and stream model
Align with server/console team on header names and server behavior expectations
Implement shared defaults in SDK spec and wire up to Python/TS/Go client libraries
Add integration tests that simulate transient network failures and stream interruptions
Create developer-facing docs and migration notes
Design a telemetry event schema to capture retry/resume occurrences for later optimization
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Agreed on three opinionated retry profiles: fast-fail, default, and throughput-friendly. Fast-fail used for non-idempotent operations by default; clients may opt-in to aggressive retries.
2025-02-18: Decided to standardize on 'Idempotency-Key' for unary requests and 'X-Resume-Token' for streaming resume tokens. Server teams asked to accept both header forms for backward compatibility.
2025-02-24: Chose 'decorrelated jitter' as the default jitter strategy (per AWS best-practices) to avoid thundering herds; multiplier 1.6 for default profile.

2025-03-01: Streaming semantics: SDK will attempt 'resume' when a server-provided resume token is available and transport classifies interruption as transient; otherwise fall back to restart. Resume is best-effort and servers must be idempotent across resumed partial operations.
notes: Rationale for separate header names: explicitness improves observability and server-side guarding; resume tokens may be opaque and not meaningful as general idempotency keys.
Edge-case: long-lived streams where resume token expiry must be documented. Servers should include token_ttl metadata when possible.
SDK ergonomics: provide automatic idempotency-key generation helpers (UUIDv4) and a developer flag to persist keys across retries for long-running user actions.
examples:
Python unary example:
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key='...')
# auto-generated idempotency key helper
resp = client.generate('complete', input='...')
# retry profile: default => initial_delay=0.08, multiplier=1.6, max_delay=2.0, attempts=5
retry_profiles: fast-fail: initial_delay=0.05, multiplier=1.4, max_delay=0.5, max_attempts=3, jitter=none - intended for non-idempotent ops or UI actions where latency matters more than retries
default: initial_delay=0.08, multiplier=1.6, max_delay=2.0, max_attempts=5, jitter=decorrelated - the recommended general-purpose profile
throughput-friendly: initial_delay=0.2, multiplier=1.6, max_delay=5.0, max_attempts=8, jitter=decorrelated - for batch workloads where a higher chance of success is preferred over latency
error_taxonomy: Transport / Network: timeouts, connection resets, transient DNS/gateway errors - generally retryable at the SDK transport layer
Transient server: 502, 503, 504, 429 (when retry-after absent) - retryable subject to server guidance and idempotency
Application-level retryable: well-known transient model-loading errors (e.g., MODEL_WARMUP) - server should signal via explicit retryable error code and SDKs map to retryable
Non-retryable: 400-series client validation errors, authentication failures (401/403), and permanent model errors - should not be retried by default
Ambiguous: 409/conflict - may be retriable only when an idempotency key semantics indicate safe reattempt; default is non-retryable unless idempotent
stream_resume_contract: Resume token lifecycle: servers issue opaque tokens with optional ttl; SDKs must persist tokens if client opts-in and attach 'X-Resume-Token' on reconnect attempts.

Resume vs Restart: SDK attempts resume when token exists AND the disconnection is classified as transient (transport-layer). If resume fails (token rejected or expired), SDK falls back to restart and surface an informative error to the developer.
Idempotency across resume: servers must guarantee that resuming a stream does not re-run non-idempotent finalizers; document server-side expectations in API docs.
Developer controls: expose flags: enableResume (default true), resumePersistence (in-memory|user-managed), and resumeBackoffProfile (default profile).

2025-02-17: Drafted header names and posted to API-standards channel; server team acknowledged and asked for backward compatibility note.
2025-02-21: Implemented prototype in python-sdk: default profile and Idempotency-Key header helper; tests added for unary retries.
2025-02-28: TS/Go teams prototyped resume token propagation and a unified telemetry ping (retry_attempt, resume_attempted, resume_succeeded).
2025-03-03: Security review kickoff scheduled; liaise with security on header exposure policy and log redaction for resume tokens.
open_questions: Should 'Retry-After' server responses always be honored even when client-specified max_attempts would otherwise continue? (proposal: yes, server guidance wins)
What is the recommended default persistence for resume tokens across environment restarts? (proposal: in-memory by default; user opt-in for durable storage)
Should the SDK surface resume tokens to end developers or keep them completely managed? (proposal: expose as opt-in and provide helpers to persist)
How to phase-roll this behavior so existing clients don’t see regressions? Need a compatibility flag with the next minor SDK release.
